name: SMA Solar Technology AG
reason: Solar inverter maker with EPS swinging from EUR 6.50 (2023) to -5.22 (2025), EBIT margin -13.1% (9th pctile) and 10y avg ROIC -2.7%; subsidy/rate-driven demand and Chinese competition make earnings unforecastable and economics poor.

name: SoftwareOne Holding Ltd.
reason: Software licensing reseller whose adjusted EPS fell from CHF 0.82 (2020) to 0.44 (2025) amid vendor (Microsoft) incentive changes and the Crayon merger; EBIT margin at a 100th-pctile 14.5% after restructuring and adjusted-vs-GAAP gap is extreme, with no durable moat.

name: Royal Unibrew A/S
reason: Well-run multi-beverage brewer with adjusted EPS DKK 13.11 to 31.40 (9.1% 10y CAGR) and consensus +9-11%/yr, but revenue doubled largely via acquisitions (Vrumona DKK 2.4bn in 2023; acq/FCF 0.52), ROIC fell from 22% (2021) to 13%, EBIT margin slid 20% to 14%, and 5y EPS CAGR is only 5.4%.

name: Rio Tinto plc
reason: Diversified miner whose earnings are set by iron ore, copper and aluminium prices (EBIT margin 13-45% range, EPS -38% in 2022, USD EPS 13.21 peak vs 6.69 now) with consensus EPS LTG ~3%; commodity earner fails the forecastability test.

name: Prosegur Compania de Seguridad SA
reason: Guarding/cash-in-transit business with adjusted EPS EUR 0.27 (2015) to 0.22 (2025), 10y avg ROIC 5.8%, net debt/EBITDA 2.8x and heavy LatAm (Brazil/Argentina) FX translation exposure; secular decline in cash usage and no specialness.

name: WH Smith PLC
reason: Travel retailer with adjusted EPS GBP 0.87 (2015) to 0.43 (2025), net debt/EBITDA 3.4x, a large adjusted-vs-GAAP gap and the 2025 North America profit overstatement; balance sheet and earnings quality fail the bar.

name: Hoegh Autoliners ASA
reason: Car-carrier shipping owner whose EBIT margin went from -0.9% (2018) to 40.9% (2024) on the vessel-supply cycle and is at the 75th pctile with consensus FY1 EPS -21%; freight-rate-driven earnings near a cyclical peak.

name: Prada S.p.A.
reason: Strong luxury brands (Miu Miu momentum) with EPS EUR 0.13 (2015) to 0.33 (2025), but the 2015-19 decline shows brand-cycle volatility, EBIT margin 22.7% is at the 82nd pctile, 10y avg ROIC is 7.8%, and the 2025 Versace acquisition adds integration risk with consensus FY1 EPS -10.8%.

name: Vesuvius Plc
reason: Steel/foundry consumables supplier tied to global steel output, with adjusted EPS GBP 0.56 (2022) to 0.34 (2025), 10y avg ROIC 5.9% and net debt/EBITDA 2.1x; cyclical and ordinary returns.

name: DSV A/S
reason: Best-in-class freight forwarder (10y EPS CAGR 15.5%), but growth is acquisition-led (acq/FCF 0.82, shares +3.2%/yr) and the transformational DB Schenker deal leaves net debt/EBITDA 3.2x, while EPS is 0.63x its DKK 81.4 2022 freight-rate peak.

name: Marks and Spencer Group plc
reason: UK clothing/food retailer with adjusted EPS GBP 0.33 (2015) to 0.23 (2025), 10y avg ROIC 2.9%, EBIT margin 2.9% (9th pctile) after the 2025 cyber attack and shares +2.1%/yr; turnaround story, not a durable compounder.

name: MAIRE S.p.A.
reason: EPC contractor with EPS EUR 0.14 to 0.80 (18.9% 10y CAGR) and net cash, but earnings depend on lumpy hydrocarbon/fertilizer project awards and fixed-price execution risk, EBIT margin is a thin 5.3% and EPS is at its 10y high.

name: Playtech PLC
reason: Gambling software firm whose adjusted EPS fell from GBP 0.29 (2018) to 0.14 (2025) with a -11.1% EBIT margin after selling Snaitech; gambling regulation and customer concentration (Caliplay dispute) are credible 5-yr threats.

name: Bravida Holding AB
reason: Nordic installation contractor with adjusted EPS SEK 6.23 (2022) to 5.88 (2025), a flat ~6% EBIT margin and bolt-on-acquisition growth tied to construction activity; cheap-but-ordinary with no moat.

name: Krones AG
reason: Beverage filling/packaging machinery leader with EPS EUR 4.94 (2015) to 9.45 (2025) record high, but 10y EPS CAGR is 6.7% including a 2019-20 collapse (EPS 1.01), margin at the 73rd pctile and ~10% ROIC in a capex-cyclical industry.

name: JCDecaux SE
reason: Outdoor advertiser with adjusted EPS EUR 1.15 (2015) to 1.26 (2025), 10y avg ROIC 3.0%, EBIT margin at a 100th-pctile 12.3% and ad-cycle plus concession-renewal risk; no growth record.

name: Lectra SA
reason: Cutting-equipment and fashion software firm whose adjusted EPS fell from EUR 1.38 (2022) to 0.69 (2025) after the Gerber deal (acq/FCF 0.79, shares +1.9%/yr); consensus +20-27%/yr recovery depends on fashion/auto capex cycles and SaaS transition.

name: Hypoport SE
reason: Europace mortgage platform has network effects, but EPS fell from EUR 4.78 (2021) to 1.77 (2024) when rates rose and EBIT margin is 4.9% vs 13.7% max; earnings are set by the German mortgage/rate cycle and acq/FCF is 1.21.

name: HAL Trust
reason: Investment holding company whose EPS swings with gains and quoted stakes (EUR 44.73 in 2021, 7.23 in 2022, 13.10 in 2024) across a mixed portfolio (optical retail, Boskalis, Vopak, real estate); look-through earnings are not forecastable from this data.

name: Telefonaktiebolaget LM Ericsson
reason: Telecom equipment vendor with revenue CAGR -0.4% over 10y, EPS SEK 5.99 (2015) to 8.51 (2025) via losses in 2017 and 2023, 10y avg ROIC 2.1%, and dependence on operator 5G capex cycles and Huawei/Nokia competition.
